content.title: Alex Hall
content.text: HometownSalt Lake City, UTEducationUniversity of UtahQuick FactsSpecialty: Slopestyle, Big AirSon of Elena Conti and Marcus HallHas an older brother, AldoGrew up in Zurich, Switzerland from age one to age 16First athlete to land a 2160 in competitionCan speak five languages (English, French, Italian, German and Swiss)Enjoys surfingBiographical InformationAlex Hall was born in Alaska but was raised in Zurich, Switzerland, from age one to age 16 where his parents were professors. Hall built rails in his backyard as a child and would practice multiple hours after school as he honed his skills to become one of the most versatile freeskiers in the world.Alex Hall would make his FIS World Cup debut at 16 and later that season represent the United States at the Youth Winter Olympics winning silver in slopestyle and finishing fourth in halfpipe. Hall made his Olympic debut at the Olympic Winter Games PyeongChang 2018, finishing 16th in the men's slopestyle. Four years later, he would win gold in slopestyle at the Olympic Winter Games Beijing 2022 based on a tremendous first run in the finals where landed a back-air "pretzel" to impress the judges. Hall is the fourth athlete to earn gold in four different disciplines at the X Games (big air, slopestyle, knuckle huck and real ski) and won the big air event in 2022 by landing the first-ever 2160 in competition.Outside of competitions, Hall is a dedicated filmmaker, capturing backcountry and urban skiing clips to showcase his inventive approach to the sport. When not skiing, he enjoys surfing.Olympic Experience3-time Olympian; 2-time Olympic medalist (1 gold, 1 silver)Olympic Games Milan 2026, silver (Slopestyle - Men), 26th (Big Air - Men)Olympic Games Beijing 2022, gold (Slopestyle - Men), 8th (Big Air - Men)Olympic Games Pyeongchang 2018, 16th (Slopestyle - Men)World Championships ExperienceMost recent: 2025 – bronze (Slopestyle - Men), 6th (Big Air - Men)Years of participation: Big Air - Men 2019, 2021, 2025; Slopestyle - Men 2017, 2019, 2021, 2025Medals: 2 (2 bronze)Bronze – 2025 (Slopestyle - Men); 2021 (Slopestyle - Men)
